ثُمَالٌ Steeped, or macerated, poison; as also ↓ مُثَمَّلٌ : (T, S, K: [in the CK, المُنْتَقِعُ is put for المُنْقَعُ:]) or ↓ the latter signifies poison that has been long steeped, and has remained: (S, * M:) or that has been steeped in a vessel, and remained steeped for some days, until it has fermented: (Ibn-'Abbád, Z:) or poison with which has been mixed something that strengthens it and excites its energy, that it may be more penetrating, or more effective: (Ham p. 215:) and simply poison. (T.) [The poison of a serpent or other thing. (Golius, from Meyd.)] ―
-b2- [Hence,] الكَرَى ↓ رَنَّحَهُ مُثَمَّلُ (tropical:) [The infection of drowsiness made him to incline from side to side]. (TA.) ―
-b3- See also ثَمَالَةٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
